target_customer: Life science companies and researchers recruiting patients and data for clinical trials, with a focus on African populations; now pharma trial teams using digital twins
problem: Clinical trials under-represent African patients and struggle with enrollment; the founder aimed to connect patients to research and later to simulate trials with digital twins.
business_model: Two-sided marketplace and SaaS platform for trial recruitment, later software for protocol rehearsal with medical digital twins
product_category: Clinical trial recruitment and digital twin software

founders.name: Melissa Bime
founders.background_notes: YC page: registered nurse who has worked with patients in healthcare settings in Africa. Fondo interview: trained as nurse in Cameroon, worked on COVID vaccine trials at Stanford.

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace and trial management software is standard; building credible medical digital twins from clinical data is harder.

defensibility.rationale: Patient communities and data can accumulate, but the early product was copyable and large trial platforms operate in the same space.

market_need_then: The founder describes a rare-disease trial enrolling a remote patient in Africa as the inspiration; no spend or regulatory data was found for 2021.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-led around patient communities; later pitch 'Run the trial before you run the trial'.

branding.brand_signature: Run the trial before you run the trial tagline

brand_strength.rationale: Hard-to-spell coined name with little press; a vendor description varies across profiles.

pivots.from: Patient community marketplace for trial recruitment in Africa
pivots.to: AI digital twin platform for rehearsing clinical trials
pivots.why: Not stated by a source. The site and Fondo interview describe the digital twin product; the year is not given and 2024 is an unverified placeholder.

outcome_analysis: Infiuss raised a small YC investment in 2021 and an undisclosed investment from UM6P Ventures reported in October 2022. It later moved from patient recruitment toward digital twin trial simulation and shows customer logos from WHO and MHRA on its site without describing the relationships. Funding figures conflict widely, so traction and runway are unknown and the outcome is still open.
notes: The pivot year is a placeholder, unverified.
